front_blocks.md: Define **fundamental particle**.

back_blocks.md: A **fundamental particle** is a particle that is not made up of any other particles.

front_blocks.md: Define **hadron**.

back_blocks.md: A **hadron** is any particle made up of quarks.

front_blocks.md: What are the charge and mass of a neutrino?

back_blocks.md: A **neutrino** has **no charge** and **negligible mass**.

front_blocks.md: **True or False?**
Leptons interact via the strong force.

back_blocks.md: **False.**
Leptons interact via the **weak interaction**, the **electromagnetic force** and the **gravitational force**, but they do **not** interact via the **strong force**.

front_blocks.md: Quarks have never been observed alone; they exist only in pairs or groups of **..........**

back_blocks.md: Quarks have never been observed alone; they exist only in pairs or groups of **three**.

cards.front_md: Quarks have never been observed alone; they exist only in pairs or groups of **..........**
cards.back_md: Quarks have never been observed alone; they exist only in pairs or groups of **three**.

front_blocks.md: Define **anti-quark**.

back_blocks.md: An **anti-quark** is the antiparticle of a quark; it is identical to the quark except with the **opposite relative charge**.

cards.front_md: Define **anti-quark**.
cards.back_md: An **anti-quark** is the antiparticle of a quark; it is identical to the quark except with the **opposite relative charge**.

front_blocks.md: What are the relative charges of an up quark and a down quark?

back_blocks.md:
- **Up quark**: +⅔ *e*
- **Down quark**: −⅓ *e*

front_blocks.md: How is the charge of a hadron determined?

back_blocks.md: The charge of a **hadron** is the **sum of the charges** of its constituent quarks.

cards.front_md: How is the charge of a hadron determined?
cards.back_md: The charge of a **hadron** is the **sum of the charges** of its constituent quarks.

front_blocks.md: A proton has quark composition **uud**, giving it a total charge of **..........**

back_blocks.md: A proton has quark composition **uud**, giving it a total charge of **+1*e***.

cards.front_md: A proton has quark composition **uud**, giving it a total charge of **..........**
cards.back_md: A proton has quark composition **uud**, giving it a total charge of **+1*e***.

front_blocks.md: What replaces quarks in the composition of anti-protons and anti-neutrons?

back_blocks.md: Anti-protons and anti-neutrons are made up of **anti-quarks** instead of quarks.

cards.front_md: What replaces quarks in the composition of anti-protons and anti-neutrons?
cards.back_md: Anti-protons and anti-neutrons are made up of **anti-quarks** instead of quarks.

front_blocks.md: **True or False?**
The charge of a hadron depends only on the number of quarks it contains, not on which flavours they are.

back_blocks.md: **False.**
The charge of a hadron depends on the **sum of the charges of its specific quarks**, and different flavours carry different relative charges.

front_blocks.md: Define **baryon**.

back_blocks.md: A **baryon** is a hadron made up of **three quarks**.

front_blocks.md: Define **meson**.

back_blocks.md: A **meson** is a hadron made up of a **quark and anti-quark pair**.

cards.back_md: A **meson** is a hadron made up of a **quark and anti-quark pair**.

front_blocks.md: What is the quark composition of a proton?

back_blocks.md: A **proton** is made up of **two up quarks and one down quark** (*uud*).

front_blocks.md: What is the quark composition of a neutron?

back_blocks.md: A **neutron** is made up of **two down quarks and one up quark** (*udd*).

cards.front_md: What is the quark composition of a neutron?
cards.back_md: A **neutron** is made up of **two down quarks and one up quark** (*udd*).

front_blocks.md: What is the quark composition of an anti-baryon?

back_blocks.md: An **anti-baryon** is made up of **three anti-quarks**.

cards.front_md: What is the quark composition of an anti-baryon?
cards.back_md: An **anti-baryon** is made up of **three anti-quarks**.

front_blocks.md: **True or False?**
A baryon can be made up of a mixture of quarks and anti-quarks.

back_blocks.md: **False.**
A baryon is made up of **either all quarks or all anti-quarks** — combinations of quarks and anti-quarks do not exist in a baryon.

back_blocks.md: All baryons and mesons have **integer (whole number)** charges, for example +1*e* or −2*e*.

front_blocks.md: Which fundamental interaction is responsible for beta decay?

back_blocks.md: Beta decay occurs via the **weak interaction**.

cards.front_md: Which fundamental interaction is responsible for beta decay?
cards.back_md: Beta decay occurs via the **weak interaction**.

front_blocks.md: Which quark transformation occurs in β<sup>-</sup> decay?

back_blocks.md: In β<sup>-</sup> decay, a **down quark** turns into an **up quark**, changing a neutron into a proton.

cards.front_md: Which quark transformation occurs in β<sup>-</sup> decay?
cards.back_md: In β<sup>-</sup> decay, a **down quark** turns into an **up quark**, changing a neutron into a proton.

front_blocks.md: Which quark transformation occurs in β<sup>+</sup> decay?

back_blocks.md: In β<sup>+</sup> decay, an **up quark** turns into a **down quark**, changing a proton into a neutron.

cards.front_md: Which quark transformation occurs in β<sup>+</sup> decay?
cards.back_md: In β<sup>+</sup> decay, an **up quark** turns into a **down quark**, changing a proton into a neutron.

front_blocks.md: In β<sup>-</sup> decay, a neutron turns into a proton, emitting an electron and an **..........**

back_blocks.md: In β<sup>-</sup> decay, a neutron turns into a proton, emitting an electron and an **anti-electron neutrino**.

cards.front_md: In β<sup>-</sup> decay, a neutron turns into a proton, emitting an electron and an **..........**
cards.back_md: In β<sup>-</sup> decay, a neutron turns into a proton, emitting an electron and an **anti-electron neutrino**.

front_blocks.md: **True or False?**
Beta decay changes the number of quarks in a nucleon.

back_blocks.md: **False.**
Beta decay involves a change in the **flavour** of one quark (down to up, or up to down), not the number of quarks — the nucleon still contains three quarks.

back_blocks.md: β<sup>+</sup> decay emits a **positron** and an **electron neutrino**.
